record.original_question: Characterize the dual binary discriminator varieties that are dually congruence distributive at their discriminating constant. More broadly, characterize pointed discriminator-variety subclasses of the class of dual binary discriminator varieties in terms of ideal-theoretic properties of their members.

evidence.quote: Characterise the class of dual binary discriminator varieties that are dually congruence distributive at their discriminating constant.
A worthwhile but as yet incomplete research program would be to characterise each pointed discriminator variety sub-class of the class of dual binary discriminator varieties

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let $\mathcal{V}$ be a variety of algebras of a fixed signature containing a distinguished constant symbol $0$. A ternary term $d(x,y,z)$ of $\mathcal{V}$ is called a dual binary discriminator (with discriminating constant $0$) on an algebra $A \in \mathcal{V}$ if, for all $a,b,c \in A$,
$$d^A(a,b,c) = \begin{cases} c & \text{if } a = b, \\ 0 & \text{if } a \neq b. \end{cases}$$
The variety $\mathcal{V}$ is called a dual binary discriminator variety if there is a single ternary term that realises the dual binary discriminator on every member of a generating class of $\mathcal{V}$ (equivalently, on a class of algebras whose generated variety is $\mathcal{V}$).

For an algebra $A$ with a constant $0$ and a congruence $\Theta \in \mathrm{Con}\,A$, write $[0]\Theta = \{a \in A : a\,\Theta\,0\}$ for the $0$-class of $\Theta$. The algebra $A$ is said to be dually congruence distributive at $0$ (equivalently, dually congruence $0$-distributive) if, for all $\Theta,\Psi,\Phi \in \mathrm{Con}\,A$,
$$[0]\bigl((\Theta \wedge \Psi) \vee \Phi\bigr) = [0]\bigl((\Theta \vee \Phi) \wedge (\Psi \vee \Phi)\bigr).$$
A variety is dually congruence distributive at its discriminating constant if every algebra in it has this property.

Problem. 
(a) Give an intrinsic (e.g. equational or ideal-theoretic) characterisation of those dual binary discriminator varieties that are dually congruence distributive at their discriminating constant $0$.
(b) More generally, for each natural subclass of pointed discriminator varieties sitting inside the class of dual binary discriminator varieties, provide a characterisation of its members in terms of ideal-theoretic properties (e.g. properties of the lattice of ideals, ideal generation, or commutator-type operations on ideals) of the algebras involved.
